problem: Most VLN approaches optimize navigation accuracy (success rate) and rarely consider path efficiency (path length), so agents take unnecessarily long routes.
motivation: Success rate and path length are equally important in VLN: the former measures accuracy and the latter efficiency. The paper argues that predicting how much navigation progress each candidate action would bring can improve both accuracy and efficiency, and that a progress monitor can supply a self-supervised signal for unseen environments.
key_idea: Predict the future navigation progress each candidate action would achieve and add it to the action distribution (Multi-Grounding Navigator), then shorten paths and add self-supervised adaptation using a progress monitor.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract claims that the progress predictor improves both accuracy and efficiency, that path-shortening further improves efficiency, and that the self-supervised module helps most in unseen environments.
method: Progress predictor: predicts the future navigation progress that would be attained by taking each candidate action.
Multi-Grounding Navigator (MGN): produces the action distribution by adding the predicted future progress to the standard grounding scores.
Path-shortening (PS): a method applied after the action distribution is given to remove redundant steps and improve path efficiency.
Self-supervised (SS) module: uses an extra progress monitor to further improve navigation performance, especially in unseen environments.

setting.backbone: not specified in abstract (learned VLN navigator with progress predictor and progress monitor)
setting.training_data: R2R dataset; self-supervised module on top (details not given in abstract)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (assumed, not stated in abstract)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (assumed, not stated in abstract)

results: The abstract states that MGN with SS and/or PS improves both accuracy and efficiency over baselines on R2R, especially in unseen environments. No numbers are given.
limitations: Details of the backbone, baselines and numerical gains are not available from the abstract alone.
